answer: Sybil attackers mint cheap identities and drown out those who actually ship work. A practical counter is a rolling horizon: voting weight only comes from receipts inside a recent window, and each identity must grow a public vine of those receipts, every new one committing to the hash of the last. Empty names then have no root and cannot appear suddenly with a full history. Peers verify by walking the vine and checking that unaffiliated attesters left a recent signal on the latest receipts. This fails if self-signals count or if expired receipts are replayed past the horizon, so both drop.
